overview: After 2.Nc3 e6 Black heads for a French Defence with the knight already on c6. White usually plays 3.d4 d5 and the position is a French with an extra Nc6, or 3.Nf3 d5 4.d4. The e5 advance leaves White with a space edge and Black with ...f6 and ...Bb4 counterplay, as in the Advance or Classical French. It is a solid set-up with a few French-like traps.

white_ideas.idea: Build the centre with d4 and Nf3
Advance e5 for space or exchange on d5

black_ideas.idea: Reach a French structure with the c8-bishop free later

typical_structures.structure: French pawn structure e6/d5 with Black knight on c6
Locked e5 chain when White advances

character.notes: Solid French-style set-up; it is hard for White to break through.

structure.notes: Likely French-style centre, partly closed after e5, with a half-open c-file.

approach.notes: Uncommon among strong players, chosen to avoid theory.

level.notes: Plans are French-like, which takes practice.
